title: GFIS Recovery
content:
ORION NanoFab Documentation
SUPERUSER ONLY

GFIS Recovery

Use this page after GFIS gun/column vacuum (UHV) was lost (full outage, chamber vent, or a vacuum event) and the column requires a bake before the source can be recovered. Vacuum restoration is covered on the Power-Up page; this page is the single home for the bake → anneal → trimer sequence.

WARNING
High voltage / restricted maintenance: follow lockout and site electrical-safety requirements. The GFIS high voltages must remain disabled while cables are unplugged for the bake.

Prepare

  1. Verify the GFIS column state is Pumped No Ion Pump; home the GFIS apertures.
  2. Unplug the accelerator, extractor, and Lens 1 high-voltage cables at the column and wrap the cables in clean Al foil for the bake (HIM open procedure, p. 4).
  3. Confirm the LN₂ supply is connected and adequate — tank pressure ~1.5 bar and the tank valve open — so the Dewar refills after the bake.

Bake

  1. In Service Machine → GFIS Column Maintenance, select Warm, Bake and Get Cold and set the hours to bake. At this site 72 h is sufficient (the ZEISS standard recommendation is 100 h — Tool-Owner-approved local value). Click Execute Now and leave it to complete.
  2. After the bake completes, reconnect the high-voltage cables (remove the Al foil).
  3. Verify the GFIS state is Pumped (GFIS ion pump on) and the gun pressure reaches ~1e-10 T — the threshold that allows helium flow for trimer formation. If the pressure does not recover, do not proceed — escalate (degas/cryosurface regeneration per the gun-overheat page, then service if it still fails).

Source recovery

  1. In Service Machine → Power Distribution → Power Supplies, enable the four GFIS high-voltage elements.
  2. Load a blank-metal sample suitable for SFIM and drive the stage to the saved SFIM stage label.
  3. From ZEN GFIS Column Maintenance, perform the Light Anneal, then the Maintain BIV source build (recommended recovery after the bake — outage transcript p. 6).
  4. Continue with trimer formation and column alignments in the normal manner (see Trimer Formation); if a trimer cannot be formed even at very high extraction, use the decrease BIV source build and record the BIV for the next formation.
